title: Minimax Precision for Median Effects under Community-Level Randomization with Binary Responses

proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived the original-record mixed-experiment transfer, terminating certified evaluator, uniformly attaining classifier, strict missing-hub floor, and equal-Kish nonrepresentation; D0.5 math and citation checks passed. The cold review and independent validity consult graded the package incremental below the field floor because optimized moderate-case values, least-favorable structure, phase boundaries, and practical evaluator execution remain unresolved. Formalization was not entered: there are no Lean proofs or promoted artifacts from this run.
tldr: A known community spectrum determines precision for binary marginal median effects beyond population size and Kish effective size. Under independent fair leader assignments and fixed interior binary response tables, the full-record minimax error converges to \(C_H(a,\rho,\eta)=V_H(a,\rho,\eta)\). Reversible local comparison, legal integer repair, unbounded-class transfer, a certified all-spectrum evaluator, and a uniformly attaining data-only classifier are proved. Every hub with \(a_h>2\rho\) forces the explicit strict bound in Lemma \ref{lem:strict-missing-hub-floor}, so its \(1/2\) missing-counterfactual subexperiment understates full-class error. The equal-Kish six-hub example has one value strictly above \(1/2\) and the other at most \(0.475340436782426\). For one hub with \(a_1>2\rho\) and \(\rho\geq12/5\), the value is strictly above \(1/2\) and at most \(0.500000396664077\). Exact moderate-margin values, the optimal excess above the explicit strict endpoint \(L_1\), optimal prior/correlation support, and action-surface phase boundaries remain unresolved. Qualifying critical spectra force limiting best worst-case correct classification probability strictly below \(1/2\). The anti-conflict interpretation is a prospective binary community-leader planning benchmark.
gap: Wang--Wang--Zhou regularizes finite-population quantiles through local CDF smoothness; Cheng--Li supplies regular cluster efficiency; Chernozhukov et al. obtain discrete-quantile coverage through CDF inversion. These results do not evaluate the declared fixed-table ternary median-effect error with unknown response pairing and missing critical-community counterfactuals.
fill: The core binds an exact count likelihood, reversible local approximation, legal integer realization, unbounded-class transfer, and certified continuum decision evaluation. The equal-Kish consequence makes the spectrum dependence observable to an experiment planner. Generic symmetry, Gaussian decision theory, and finite optimization receive antecedent credit. The evaluator returns a verified error interval and a classifier for that public census. The one-hub near-floor region and the equal-Kish comparison show when singleton expansion cannot replace information about a large community counterfactual.
